So I have looked at the general surface of section of the simple model. I have checked the limits, $E \to -\infty$ and $E\to+\infty$ as well as a particular interesting region between $-0.53 > E > -0.3$ in units of $|C/L|$ where $L_1=L_2=L$.

In the region $-\infty< E/[|C/L|] < -1.0$ the surface of section shows a mixed phase space. Partially cahotic and partially regular.

Here we can see that the translation through the energy Intervals behaves like a linear transformation of the surface of section. The dynamics is invariant under rescaling.

What I am trying to find the words for is this mathematical property of the system:

$$\lambda H(p,q) = \tilde{H}(\tilde{p},\tilde{q})$$

$$\dot{\tilde{x}} =  S\frac{\partial \tilde{H}}{\partial \tilde{x}}$$

$$\begin{pmatrix} \dot{\tilde{p}} \\ \dot{\tilde{q}} \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} - \frac{\partial \tilde{H}}{\partial \tilde{q}} \\ \frac{\partial \tilde{H}}{\partial \tilde{p}} \end{pmatrix}$$

with the transformation $\tilde{p} = \sqrt{\lambda} p$, $\tilde{q} = \sqrt{\lambda} q$ and $\lambda = \frac{1}{|C/L|}$.

$$\Rightarrow \Phi(\tilde{t},\tilde{x}) =  \Phi(t,x)$$
